item.title: Has bird flu killed millions of chickens in Colorado?
item.description: Yes. Avian flu outbreaks have led to the deaths of more than 11 million commercial chickens in Colorado since 2022.

item.title: Colorado is losing 1 affordable housing unit for every 2 it builds. But the state keeps rejecting efforts to stop the bleeding.
item.description: Gov. Jared Polis and state housing officials have prioritized new construction over preserving existing affordable rental housing.

item.title: Feds plan to remove 1,100 more wild horses from Colorado this summer, citing wildfires and drought
item.description: Two of the three roundups will use helicopters, despite requests from state officials for more “humane” solutions

item.title: Colorado’s growing share of unaffiliated voters is making it harder for candidates to get on the ballot
item.description: Democratic and Republican candidates collecting signatures to make their party’s primary ballot can only collect signatures from voters in their party. With unaffiliated voters now making up half of the statewide electorate, partisans are harder to find.

item.title: Wildfire south of Colorado Springs grows to 7,300 acres as crews gain some containment
item.description: Fire crews were able to start “boxing in” the 24 fire overnight but state highway will remain closed through this week

item.title: Opinion: Colorado bill that would extend infant abandonment window is misguided
item.description: House Bill 1024 is a solution looking for a problem and undermines best practices in adoption.

item.title: Shannon Bird’s “no” votes on some big Democratic bills may both help and hurt her run for Congress
item.description: The former state representative is taking heat in the 8th Congressional District Democratic primary for her votes on immigration bills and funding questions

item.title: As the BLM in Moab opens hundreds of miles of trails to e-bikes, Colorado land managers also weigh expansion
item.description: The BLM’s Colorado River Valley Field Office is reviewing a plan to open 220 miles of trails to e-bikes in Eagle, Pitkin, Garfield counties

item.title: Colorado lawmakers step in — again — to urge federal action on stalled tribal water access
item.description: The Southern Ute and Ute Mountain Ute officials have pushed for federal action on water projects for years. Colorado lawmakers join in the fight.

item.title: Colorado man released by Afghanistan after being detained for more than a year
item.description: Dennis Coyle is an academic researcher who was detain in January 2025. Afghan authorities said he broke laws, but never said which ones.
